summary: The EU lists Greece among the Schengen area countries. EU law says Member States let Union citizens enter with a valid identity card or passport and may impose no entry visa on them; the EEA Agreement extends this to nationals of the EFTA States, and the EU–Swiss free movement agreement lets Swiss nationals enter on a valid identity card or passport. Nationals of the countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries listed in Annex I must hold a visa; ETIAS is currently not in operation. The Visa Code sets the visa fee at €90, and the Greek Embassy in London says applications for Greek visas must be submitted through the Global Visa Center World offices.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Greece?
faq.answer: No visa is needed for a short stay: the United States is among the countries whose nationals Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 exempts from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. ETIAS, which will require visa-exempt travellers to have a travel authorisation, is currently not in operation; its website lists a EUR 20 application fee.

faq.question: How much does a Greece Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Visa Code sets the visa fee at €90, and €45 for children from the age of six and below the age of 12; the fee is waived for children under six. The Greek Embassy in London lists the Schengen visa type A or C at €90 and visas for children under the age of 12 as free.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Greece?
faq.answer: ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The EU's ETIAS website lists a EUR 20 fee, from which applicants under 18 or above 70 years of age are exempt, and says an authorisation is valid for up to three years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.

faq.question: Does Greece have a digital nomad visa?
faq.answer: Greece's foreign ministry says the consular authority decides on applications from digital nomads (category Z.1) within 10 days from submission. A national type D visa covers entry and stay for a period exceeding 90 days and up to 365 days, and the Greek Embassy in London lists the national long-stay (type D) visa at €180. No official source we could read states the income requirement.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Greece without a visa?
faq.answer: Nationals of the countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. The UK government tells British travellers visiting other Schengen countries as well to keep the whole visit within the 90-day visa-free limit, counting visits to Schengen countries within the previous 180 days.
